left-click-action.tooltip: Show the menu: left and right click open a panel menu, with an 'Open <application>' entry added on top where it is useful. Activate directly: left click acts like a normal tray (it activates the icon) and menus contain only what the application itself provides. Middle click triggers the secondary action, Ctrl+right click opens the applet's own context menu.

right-click-native.description: Right click opens the application's own menu when it can't be translated
right-click-native.tooltip: For XApp icons and StatusNotifier items without a dbusmenu, the menu exists only inside the application. Left click still shows the 'Open …' menu.

hidden-icons.tooltip: Icons whose application name, title, id or icon name contains any of these words are hidden.

hide-open-for.description: Never show 'Open' for these icons (comma separated)
hide-open-for.tooltip: Icons whose application name, title, id or icon name contains any of these words get no 'Open' entry.

autohide-enabled.description: Move icons that are not used to a hidden icons menu
autohide-enabled.tooltip: Icons you haven't clicked for a while move to a menu behind an arrow button next to the tray icons. Using an icon from that menu shows it in the panel for a while (see below); its 'Move to the panel' button brings it back (it hides again once unused for the time set below). Ctrl+right click an icon (or right click the arrow button) for 'Hide now' and 'Pin to the panel', which keeps an icon in the panel for good.

autohide-hours.description: Hide icons that have not been used for
autohide-hours.tooltip: Only time the computer is in use counts: time asleep, or without keyboard or mouse activity for more than 5 minutes, is not counted.

autohide-visit-minutes.description: After using a hidden icon, keep it in the panel for (0 = only while in use)
autohide-visit-minutes.tooltip: Using an icon from the hidden icons menu shows it in the panel without bringing it back. With 0 it returns to the hidden icons as soon as its menu or popup closes; otherwise it stays in the panel for this many minutes (only minutes the computer is in use count). To bring an icon back, use the 'Move to the panel' button next to it in the hidden icons menu, or 'Keep in the panel' in its Tray icon submenu while it is shown.

autohide-button-position.description: Position of the hidden icons button

autohide-menu-items.description: Add a 'Tray icon' submenu (hide / pin to the panel) to icon menus
autohide-menu-items.tooltip: Added at the bottom of the menus this applet shows for the icons. Icons whose menu is drawn by the application itself don't get it; Ctrl+right click such an icon for the same options.

autohide-show-all.description: Bring all hidden icons back to the panel

reset-learned.description: Forget what was learned about icons, clear stored menus and reset the icon order
